chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the menstruating woman praying upon the deceased. He said: 'Yes, and she should not form a row with them.'
ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman pray Salat al-Janazah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that menstruation does not invalidate a woman's participation in Salat al-Janazah, distinguishing it from the ritual purity required for the individual Fard prayer. The specific condition of not standing in a row (saff) with the congregation reflects the scholarly view that while her prayer is valid, she remains in a state of minor impurity (hadath al-akbar) that precludes joining the formal communal formation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad Bin Isa, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the menstruating woman, ‘Can she pray Salaat upon the deceased?’. Heasws said: ‘Yes, and she should not form a row along with them’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad ibn ‘Isa from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who experiences Hayd (menses) if she can perform Salah (prayer) for a deceased. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, but she must not stand in the line of the others.’”
